name: Lombok Strait
genZNote: Lombok is the deep-water workaround — too big for Malacca's shallow limits, some of the largest tankers reroute all the way here instead.

sections.heading: 🚨 Location & What It Connects
bullets: A strait between the Indonesian islands of Bali and Lombok.
Connects the Java Sea/Flores Sea area to the Indian Ocean, further east and south than the Sunda Strait.
Deeper than both the Strait of Malacca and the Sunda Strait, which matters for one specific type of ship.

sections.heading: ⚓ Why It Matters
bullets: Its greater depth makes it usable by very large crude carriers (VLCCs) that are too deep-drafted to safely pass through the shallower Strait of Malacca.
An important alternative route for oil tankers moving between the Middle East and East Asia when draft restrictions matter.
Also lies along the Wallace Line, a notable biogeographic boundary separating distinct Asian and Australian wildlife zones.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Lombok Strait, between Bali and Lombok, is a deep-water Indonesian passage used by large tankers too deep-drafted for the Strait of Malacca.
keyFacts: Connects the Indian Ocean to Indonesia's inner seas.
Deeper than Malacca and Sunda — used by very large crude carriers (VLCCs).
Lies along the Wallace Line (a biogeographic boundary).
commonConfusion: Depth is the key differentiator here — Lombok isn't chosen for being shorter, but for being deep enough for ships Malacca can't handle.

highYieldFacts: Lombok Strait: between Bali and Lombok; deepest of the Indonesian alternative straits.
Used by VLCCs too large for the Strait of Malacca.
commonTraps: Don't confuse 'deepest' (Lombok) with 'busiest' (Malacca) — they're chosen for different reasons.
mustRemember: Lombok Strait = the deep-draft alternative to Malacca for the largest tankers.
